newsitem.title: USA: Alyeska idles pipeline pump station.
newsitem.headline: Alyeska idles pipeline pump station.

text.p: The operator of the trans-Alaska pipeline on Tuesday idled one of the pump stations along the 800-mile system, a move made possible by reduced oil throughput.
Alyeska Pipeline Service Co, the system's operator, said it put Pump Station 2 into standby status Tuesday morning.
The station, 57 miles south of Prudhoe Bay, will be isolated from the rest of pipeline system over the next three months, Alyeska spokeswoman Tracy Green said.
The station could be restarted within six months' notice if new oil production makes its pumping power necessary, Green said.
Oil flow through the pipeline is averaging 1.35 million barrels a day, down from the 2.0 million-barrel-a-day peak hit in 1988, Green said.
Pump Station 2 is the third of the system's 11 operations stations to be idled in a strategy to cope with declining North Slope oil production.
Alyeska put Stations 8 and 10, in the southern half of the system, into standby status last summer.
Another site near the Yukon River, Pump Station 6, is scheduled to be idled in August.
All could be restarted if needed, Alyeska said.

While the company has closed pump stations -- facilities that help push oil down the line to the Valdez marine terminal -- it expects throughput to increase in the next few years as new North Slope oil production starts, Alyeska President Bob Malone said Monday.
Alyeska expects daily oil flow to average 1.5 million barrels in 2000 and to remain at that level for several years, Malone told the Anchorage chamber of commerce.
For the present, however, Alyeska's plans concern oil-flow reductions.
Next week, the company plans to excavate a buried pipeline section near Thompson Pass, the mountainous area north of Valdez, to allow inspection for damage.
The steep Thompson Pass section was recently stricken by episodes of pipeline shaking attributed to reduced oil flow and the resulting downhill cascading effect.
Since January, Alyeska since January has used backpressure to halt the tremors. The excavation will allow officials to check on a dents in the area and possible metal fatigue, the company said.
The work will not affect pipeline throughput, Green said.
"There will be no shutdown or change in flow due to the Thompson Pass excavation," she said.
